asserts: A v1 reader reads EXACTLY version 1 and rejects every other value, and rejects block_samples that is zero or not a multiple of branching_factor, any must-understand feature bit it does not know, a profile byte outside {0, 2}, any recipe byte outside the registry, and a moment-stream feature bit that disagrees with how the blocks are framed — while skipping may-ignore feature bits it does not know.
source: the version-1 header and framing rules
contract: A reader that accepts a malformed file produces wrong answers where it should have produced an error.
notes: Each case is a well-formed file with one field patched and the rejection class it must trigger. Two of them are ACCEPTING cases — a may-ignore feature bit, and a tick rate at exactly the largest legal value — because a bound pinned only where it fails is half pinned: a reader that refuses the boundary passes every rejection here and still refuses valid files.

cases.name: v1-version-must-be-exactly-1
cases.reason: the wire version of this format is 1. A version-1 reader reads EXACTLY 1 and rejects every other value. The error should name the version it found, because a user holding a file this reader cannot read needs to know what they are holding

cases.name: v1-version-zero
cases.reason: zero is not a version; it is what an uninitialised or truncated header reads as

cases.name: v1-version-unassigned
cases.reason: no version other than 1 is assigned, so a file claiming any of them is refused rather than read on a guess

cases.name: v1-block-samples-zero
cases.reason: block_samples that is zero is rejected

cases.name: v1-block-samples-not-multiple-of-bf
cases.reason: 300 is not a multiple of branching_factor 256; the block-length parameter requires a multiple so that a level k+1 block is built from exactly branching_factor complete level k blocks and position chaining is unchanged

cases.name: v1-profile-unassigned-1
cases.reason: the profile is 0 (none) or 2 (recipe); 1 is not assigned and a file carrying it is rejected rather than guessed at

cases.name: v1-profile-unknown
cases.reason: the v1 profile is 0 (none) or 2 (recipe); nothing else

cases.name: v1-empty-file
cases.reason: zero bytes is the commonest damaged file there is — a create that never wrote, a copy that never ran. It is refused for being too short to hold a header, not for a magic that was never there to mismatch

cases.name: v1-file-shorter-than-header
cases.reason: half a header. A reader that unpacks fields before checking the length reads whatever follows the buffer

cases.name: v1-file-one-byte-short-of-header
cases.reason: the boundary, and the one an off-by-one gets wrong: 127 bytes is not a header and 128 is. A reader comparing with > rather than >= accepts this and reads one byte past the end

cases.name: v1-magic-mismatch
cases.reason: the sixth byte of the magic is part of it. A reader that matches only the five ASCII bytes accepts a file whose format marker says something else, and then reads it as version 1

cases.name: v1-branching-factor-below-2
cases.reason: a branching factor of 1 gives a level that is its own parent, so the pyramid never terminates. The specification says two or more and the reader has always refused it; nothing pinned it until now

cases.name: v1-file-state-unknown
cases.reason: file_state is 0 sealed or 1 active and there is no third value. A reader that treats anything non-zero as active reads an unknown state as one it happens to know

cases.name: v1-num-groups-zero
cases.reason: every channel belongs to a group and a group carries the time base, so a file with no groups has no way to say when any sample was taken

cases.name: v1-num-channels-zero
cases.reason: a file with no channels holds no data. It is refused rather than read as an empty success, because the likelier cause is a header written before the channels were

cases.name: v1-group-table-offset-out-of-bounds
cases.reason: the group table is refused for ending past the end of the file, which is a stated rule, rather than for whatever a reader's language does when it indexes past a buffer

cases.name: v1-channel-table-offset-out-of-bounds
cases.reason: the same rule for the channel table. Both offsets are u64 and neither is bounded by anything but the file's own length

cases.name: v1-sample-rate-zero
cases.reason: a rate of zero makes the time of sample i a division by zero, so every timestamp in the group is undefined rather than merely wrong

cases.name: v1-sample-rate-negative
cases.reason: a negative rate runs the group's time backwards, so sample i+1 precedes sample i and any search over the axis is unsound

cases.name: v1-sample-rate-nan
cases.reason: a NaN rate makes every derived timestamp compare equal to nothing, including itself, which is worse than an error because a reader finds no sample rather than failing to look

cases.name: v1-sample-rate-infinite
cases.reason: an infinite rate collapses every sample onto the group's start timestamp. It is refused with the other three because the rule is one rule: the rate is positive and finite

cases.name: v1-timing-mode-unknown
cases.reason: timing_mode is 0 fixed or 1 variable. It decides which streams a block carries and how its first stream is read, so a reader that defaults an unknown value parses every block in the group wrongly

cases.name: v1-timing-flags-reserved-bit-set
cases.reason: bits 2 to 7 of the timing-flag byte are reserved AND rejected, which is the one exception to reserved fields being ignored: these bits change how the group is read, so a reader that skips one it does not know reads the group wrongly rather than incompletely. Stated since version 1 and enforced all along; this is the case that pins it

cases.name: v1-block-extent-past-eof
cases.reason: file_offset + compressed_size reaches past the end of the file. This is checked before the CRC, because computing a CRC over a range that does not exist is the read the rule is there to prevent

cases.name: v1-block-file-offset-past-eof
cases.reason: the same rule reached by moving the start rather than the length. One rule, one class: a reader needs to know the block is not in the file, not which of the two numbers was wrong

cases.name: v1-unknown-must-understand-feature-bit
cases.reason: bit 31 is in the must-understand half and version 1 assigns it nothing, so a reader refuses the file rather than reading it as though the feature were absent. Taken with its two neighbours this is the whole rule in three cases: bit 0 is must-understand and KNOWN, so the file is accepted and the bit is acted on — it is what says whether the moment stream is there; bit 31 is must-understand and unknown, so the file is refused; bit 32 is may-ignore and unknown, so the file is accepted and the bit skipped. The patched value here keeps bit 0 set because the base file carries moments, so the only thing wrong with it is the bit a reader does not know

cases.name: v1-unknown-may-ignore-feature-bit-is-ACCEPTED
cases.reason: the HIGH 32 bits are may-ignore. This is the case that proves the split is real: the same field, a different half, and the opposite outcome. A reader that refuses both has no forward compatibility at all; a reader that accepts both has no safety

cases.name: v1-moment-stream-flag-clear-but-block-has-three-streams
cases.reason: the file's numeric level-1 blocks are framed with three streams, and clearing bit 0 says there are two. A reader must not decide the bit is stale and read the block anyway, nor decide the block is stale and trust the bit: it cannot tell which of the two is the damage, and either guess silently hands back a moment stream read as values, or values read as a truncated block

cases.name: v1-moment-stream-flag-set-but-block-has-two-streams
cases.reason: the same rule from the other side: the bit promises a moment stream the blocks do not carry. This is the direction that corrupts a reader quietly rather than loudly — it reads the values stream's length prefix as the values stream, and then reads whatever follows as moments. The file that proves the rule is the one file in the set written without moments, which is also why it is kept

cases.name: v1-decoded-size-smaller-than-index-entry
cases.reason: the index entry promises one byte fewer than the values stream decodes to. A reader that trusts the entry allocates short and either truncates the block or walks off the end of it; a reader that trusts the stream silently disagrees with the index it will use to seek. Neither is a reading of this file, so it is refused

cases.name: v1-decoded-size-larger-than-index-entry
cases.reason: the same disagreement from the other side, and the one a writer is likelier to produce: the entry was written before the stream was encoded and never corrected. Feature bit 0 still agrees with the framing here, so this fails at the decoded length and not before it

cases.name: v1-sample-count-disagrees-with-block-shape
cases.reason: the same rule from the shape's side rather than the byte count's. sample_count is the block's row count at its own level, so it fixes the decoded size of EVERY stream in the block; one more row than the block holds and no stream is the length its shape implies. A reader can refuse this before it decodes anything, by comparing uncompressed_size with the shape, or after decoding, by comparing the bytes. It is one rule, so it is one class either way

cases.name: v1-decoded-size-mismatch-at-profile-2
cases.reason: the rule exists for this profile, so this is the case that proves it. Here there is no length arithmetic to catch the disagreement earlier — the values stream is compressed, so its decoded length is not knowable until it has been decoded, and comparing that length with the index entry is the only check a profile-2 reader has on the block's size

cases.name: v1-stream-length-prefix-exceeds-block
cases.reason: a stream's u32 length prefix that runs past the block's compressed_size must be refused before any decode. With k streams there are k-1 such prefixes and each is a rejection site

cases.name: v1-stream-length-prefix-zero
cases.reason: a length of 0 leaves no room for the stream's own recipe byte, so it cannot describe a well-formed stream; the minimum is 1

cases.name: v1-stream-length-prefixes-leave-no-last-stream
cases.reason: the prefixes of the first k-1 streams must leave at least one byte for the last stream, which has no prefix and runs to compressed_size. Prefixes summing to the whole block describe a block with no values

cases.name: v1-tick-rate-numer-zero
cases.reason: with TIMEBASE_PRESENT set, a numerator of zero makes every tick the same instant; the field is >= 1 or the group is malformed

cases.name: v1-tick-rate-denom-zero
cases.reason: a denominator of zero is a division by zero in both tick conversions; the field is >= 1 or the group is malformed

cases.name: v1-tick-rate-numer-exceeds-2p32
cases.reason: both rate fields are at most 2^32. That bound is what lets an implementation evaluate the tick conversions in 128-bit integers rather than arbitrary precision: the widest intermediate is |ticks - anchor| * 10^9 * denom, below 2^125 for |ticks - anchor| < 2^63 and denom <= 2^32

cases.name: v1-tick-rate-at-2p32-is-ACCEPTED
cases.reason: 2^32 is the largest legal value, not the first illegal one. This is the case that makes the bound inclusive: a reader that treats it as exclusive refuses a valid file and passes every rejection case above

cases.name: v1-tick-rate-denom-exceeds-2p32
cases.reason: the same bound on the denominator, which is the field the widest intermediate is actually multiplied by

cases.name: v1-unknown-recipe-0x04
cases.reason: every value outside {0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03} and the 0xF0-0xFF experimental range is reserved and rejected with an actionable error naming the byte; there is no registry escape

cases.name: v1-unknown-recipe-0x7f
cases.reason: every value outside {0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03} and the 0xF0-0xFF experimental range is reserved and rejected with an actionable error naming the byte; there is no registry escape

cases.name: v1-unknown-recipe-0xef
cases.reason: every value outside {0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03} and the 0xF0-0xFF experimental range is reserved and rejected with an actionable error naming the byte; there is no registry escape

cases.name: v1-unknown-recipe-0xff
cases.reason: every value outside {0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03} and the 0xF0-0xFF experimental range is reserved and rejected with an actionable error naming the byte; there is no registry escape

cases.name: v1-profile0-with-non-identity-recipe
cases.reason: under profile 0 EVERY recipe byte must be 0x00. A profile-0 file carrying a zstd recipe is the file that would make the stdlib-only reference reader need a codec, which is the whole point of the profile
